## 6. Editor ↔ sources — the linkage is very thin

Four connections exist, all weak:

1. **Draft text → research (one-way, implicit).** `twyne-editor.tsx` emits `twyne:content` (`DraftContentDetail { html, text, wordCount }`); `onDraftChanged(text)` feeds the background watcher. The watcher reads the draft; the draft never learns what came back.

This is the closest thing to a citation link — but it is a plain string with no ProseMirror position, no mark, no id in the document. Edit the sentence and the association silently dies. 3. **`citedUrls` — string matching.** Both apparatus surfaces compute:
   ```ts
   const citedUrls = new Set(store.citations.map(c => c.lookupUrl).filter(Boolean).map(u => u.replace(/\/+$/, "")));
   // ...
   const isCited = citedUrls.has(entry.url.replace(/\/+$/, ""));
   ```
   That is the entire "is this source cited?" mechanism — a trailing-slash-normalized URL string compare against regex-detected URLs in the draft. It only works for sources whose URL was literally pasted into the manuscript.

   ```ts
   const citeInDraft = $(async (entry: BibEntry) => {
     const text = footnoteCite(entry, store.style);
     await navigator.clipboard?.writeText(text);
     window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("twyne:insert-text", { detail: text }));
   });
   ```
   Consumed by `src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx:1575`. It inserts **plain text** — e.g. `(Smith 2024)` — with no mark, no attribute, no entry id. Once inserted, nothing connects that text back to the `BibEntry`. This is the *only* source→editor write path, and the standalone `/apparatus/` route doesn't even have it.

**There is no citation mark or citation node.** The registered editor extensions are: StarterKit, ImageNode, table extensions, Placeholder, Highlight, Underline, Sub/Superscript, TextStyleKit, LineHeight, ParagraphFormat, TextAlign, TiptapLink, Typography, TaskList/TaskItem, CommentMark, PersonaNoteMark, SuggestionMark, MermaidDiagram, InlineNoteNode, RemoteCursors, MarkAnchorWidgets, Indent. Nothing citation-aware.

**Export** does join them, but only at the end: `src/utils/folio-export.ts` bundles `{ html, bibliography (filtered to folio), apparatusSettings, marginalia }`, and `src/utils/exchange.ts` extracts `<sup data-type="endnote|footnote">` nodes into "Notes"/"Footnotes" sections rendered ahead of the bibliography.

## Summary: exists vs. doesn't

**Exists**
- Two dossier routes (create, refine), form + conversational modes, AI drift report, start-over
- `BibEntry` as a full source model with provenance, target back-reference, and snippet
- A complete background research pipeline with live per-claim progress streaming
- Four pluggable research provider paths (BYOK search API, model web search, MCP, hosted Convex)
- Two near-duplicate bibliography UIs (`/apparatus/` route + `CitationsPanel` editor panel)
- Lix-blob-in-IndexedDB persistence with Convex sync (`bibliographyEntries` table)
- MLA/APA/Chicago formatters, dedupe by normalized URL, AI summarize, AI missing-claim detection
- A mature manuscript annotation system: comment / persona-note / suggestion marks, endnotes/footnotes, shared anchor-widget infrastructure
- MCP knowledge-base resource listing and reading

**Does not exist**
- Any "sources" view under `/dossier/` — the dossier is the brief, full stop
- Any canvas / graph / node / spatial UI, and **no library for one is installed** (d3/cytoscape are mermaid transitives only)
- Any annotation, note, highlight, or excerpt on a source (`BibEntry.note` is declared and entirely unused)
- Any durable link between a draft passage and a source — `target.anchor` is a fragile verbatim string; `isCited` is a URL string compare
- A citation mark/node in the editor schema; `citeInDraft` inserts inert plain text
- Any promotion flow for `accepted` (background entries are written `accepted: false` and stay that way)
- Any relationship *between* sources (no clustering, no grouping, no ordering beyond `provenance` split)

**Convex `Source` shape** (`convex/research.ts:22-30`) — what providers return before becoming a `BibEntry`: `{ title, url, snippet, author?, publisher?, date?, why? }`. Providers: tinyfish / exa / tavily / brave / serper / custom, selected by env var.

---

## 3. `src/routes/apparatus/index.tsx` (1345 lines)

Standalone full-page route at `/apparatus/`, titled "The Apparatus." Entirely hand-rolled markup — **no shared UI component library at all**, just Qwik `component$` + Tailwind + CSS variables + `useStylesScoped$` (the scoped styles define `.card`, `.row`, `.empty`, `.agent-pill`, `.cited-pill`, `.style-toggle`, `.status-dot`, `.slide-in`, `.page-turn`).

Layout, top to bottom:
1. **Status card** (~line 516) — pulsing status dot, phase headline, last query, provider, a big count of background finds, error + retry, then "Live — researching these claims" (`store.research.progress`) and "Recent research" (`store.research.activity`, max 6).
2. **Two-column grid** `grid lg:grid-cols-[1fr_1.4fr]` (line 747):
   - **Left: "Found by the agents"** (line 749) — `backgroundEntries` = `activeBibliography.filter(b => b.provenance === "background")`. Each row shows title + `agent` pill + optional `cited` pill, URL, formatted citation, `for: "<target.anchor>" · <kind>`, `why: <backgroundQuery>`, and hover actions `⌖ open` / `✕ drop`.
   - **Right: "Your bibliography"** (line 858) — `writerEntries` = everything else. MLA/APA/Chicago toggle, "Copy all", per-entry `✦ summarize` (→ `runClientSourceSummarize` → `SourceSummarizeResult { summary, keyClaims, relevanceScore, provider }`) and `✕ drop`. Below it, **"Detected in the manuscript"** listing `DetectedCitation`s with `+ add to bib`.
3. **"Missing citations"** (line 1099, gated on `apparatusSettings.flagMissingSources`) — `runClientMissingSourceDetect` returns `claims: [{ claim, reason, suggestedQuery }]`.
4. **"Knowledge bases"** (line 1191) — MCP resources from `listMcpDocuments`.
5. **Embed overlay** (line 1252) — fixed-position modal; MCP docs render as `<pre>`, web URLs as a sandboxed `<iframe>`.

**Important:** there is a near-duplicate of this surface as an in-editor panel: **`/home/diogenes/Projects/twyne/src/components/citations/citations-panel.tsx` (41 KB, ~1030 lines)**, header "Sources & Sourcerers" / "The Apparatus." It's mounted as right-panel `"citations"` in `src/routes/editor/index.tsx:1577` (panel label "Apparatus", numeral IV, accent `--color-periwinkle`, defined at :843-848). The two files duplicate a large amount of logic (bibliography loading, research snapshot polling, citation formatting, embed overlay). The panel has one thing the route lacks: `citeInDraft`.

---

## 4. Canvas / graph / spatial UI — **none exists, and no library is available**

I checked `package.json` and `bun.lock` for react-flow, xyflow, tldraw, d3, force-graph, cytoscape, konva, fabric, excalidraw, vis-network, sigma, pixi, three, jointjs, gojs, dagre, elkjs.

**Direct dependencies: zero matches.** Nothing spatial is a declared dependency.

**Transitive only:** `d3`, `d3-force`, `cytoscape`, and `khroma` appear in `bun.lock` — these are pulled in by **`mermaid@^11.15.0`**, which is used solely for `src/components/editor/extensions/mermaid-node.ts` (an atom Tiptap node that renders a Mermaid diagram from a `source` string inside the manuscript). They are not importable as a supported API surface and there is no `@types/d3` in devDependencies (only transitively). Do not plan around these.

**Grep for spatial UI in `src/`:** no `react-flow` / `xyflow` / `tldraw` / `force-graph` / `cytoscape` / `excalidraw` / `mindmap` / `d3-force` references at all.

The only `<canvas>`/`getContext` hits are incidental: `src/components/editor/extensions/pagination.ts` (text measurement), `src/utils/generation-stream.ts`, `src/components/editor/test-harness.ts`. Only "draggable" hits are Tiptap node configs (`mermaid-node.ts`, `image-node.ts`, `page-break-node.ts`) and `section-reorder.ts` (reordering document sections, list-based, not spatial).

**Conclusion: a canvas/graph feature would require adding a new dependency from scratch.** The app is a document-centric, panel-based UI: a paginated Tiptap editor with a right-hand tabbed sidebar (Cast / Rubric / Marginalia / Apparatus).

---

## 5. Annotations / notes today

There is a rich annotation system — **but it annotates the manuscript, never a source.**

Three overlapping mark types, all Tiptap marks so they serialize into the folio HTML:

| Mark | File | Purpose | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `commentMark` | `src/components/editor/extensions/comment-mark.ts` | Writer's own marginalia | `Comment` (`src/types/index.ts:434-444`): `{ id, text, selectedText, from, to, author, timestamp, resolved, replies }` |
| `personaNote` | `src/components/editor/extensions/persona-note-mark.ts` | An AI editor persona's margin note | `PersonaFeedback` (`src/types/index.ts:58-83`): `{ personaId, feedback, anchor, noteId, type, origin: "convened"\|"background" }` |
| `suggestion` | `src/components/editor/extensions/suggestion-mark.ts` | Proposed rewrite, Lix-branch-backed | `Suggestion` (`src/types/index.ts:648-...`): `{ original, replacement, rationale, versionId, status }` |

Plus **inline notes**: `EndnoteNode` (`extensions/endnote-node.ts`) — an inline atom with `{ text, kind: "endnote"|"footnote" }`, numbering derived from document order at render time (`src/components/editor/note-editing.ts:collectInlineNotes`), and an editing popover in `extensions/inline-note-popover.ts`.

**`src/components/editor/extensions/mark-anchor-widgets.ts`** is the shared anchoring mechanism — a ProseMirror plugin that paints a hit-testable chip at the end of each contiguous run of comment-like marks, carrying `data-anchor-kind` (`note|comment|suggestion`) and `data-anchor-id`. Its header comment explains why a widget beats a CSS pseudo-element. This is the extension point if you wanted a fourth annotation kind.

`Highlight` from `@tiptap/extension-highlight` is registered but is plain text highlighting, not annotation.

**What does NOT exist:** there is no annotation, note, or highlight attached to a `BibEntry`. The only per-source writer text is `BibEntry.note?` — declared in the interface, documented as "Writer's working note — never formatted into the citation", and **never read or written by any UI**. Same for `citationKey?` and `pageHint?`. There is no per-source highlight, no excerpt capture from a source, and no way to link a passage in a source to a passage in the draft.

---

## 6. Editor ↔ sources — the linkage is very thin

Four connections exist, all weak:

1. **Draft text → research (one-way, implicit).** `twyne-editor.tsx` emits `twyne:content` (`DraftContentDetail { html, text, wordCount }`); `onDraftChanged(text)` feeds the background watcher. The watcher reads the draft; the draft never learns what came back.

2. **`BibEntry.target.anchor` — a verbatim string, not a position.** When an agent finds a source, it records `ResearchTargetRef { kind, anchor, query, reason }` where `anchor` is the passage copied verbatim (capped at `MAX_ANCHOR_CHARS = 200`). This is the closest thing to a citation link — but it is a plain string with no ProseMirror position, no mark, no id in the document. Edit the sentence and the association silently dies. The Apparatus renders it as display text only (`for: "…"`).

3. **`citedUrls` — string matching.** Both apparatus surfaces compute:
   ```ts
   const citedUrls = new Set(store.citations.map(c => c.lookupUrl).filter(Boolean).map(u => u.replace(/\/+$/, "")));
   // ...
   const isCited = citedUrls.has(entry.url.replace(/\/+$/, ""));
   ```
   That is the entire "is this source cited?" mechanism — a trailing-slash-normalized URL string compare against regex-detected URLs in the draft. It only works for sources whose URL was literally pasted into the manuscript.

4. **`citeInDraft` — clipboard + a text-insert event.** `src/components/citations/citations-panel.tsx:297-307`:
   ```ts
   const citeInDraft = $(async (entry: BibEntry) => {
     const text = footnoteCite(entry, store.style);
     await navigator.clipboard?.writeText(text);
     window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("twyne:insert-text", { detail: text }));
   });
   ```
   Consumed by `src/components/editor/twyne-editor.tsx:1575`. It inserts **plain text** — e.g. `(Smith 2024)` — with no mark, no attribute, no entry id. Once inserted, nothing connects that text back to the `BibEntry`. This is the *only* source→editor write path, and the standalone `/apparatus/` route doesn't even have it.

**There is no citation mark or citation node.** The registered editor extensions are: StarterKit, ImageNode, table extensions, Placeholder, Highlight, Underline, Sub/Superscript, TextStyleKit, LineHeight, ParagraphFormat, TextAlign, TiptapLink, Typography, TaskList/TaskItem, CommentMark, PersonaNoteMark, SuggestionMark, MermaidDiagram, InlineNoteNode, RemoteCursors, MarkAnchorWidgets, Indent. Nothing citation-aware.

**Export** does join them, but only at the end: `src/utils/folio-export.ts` bundles `{ html, bibliography (filtered to folio), apparatusSettings, marginalia }`, and `src/utils/exchange.ts` extracts `<sup data-type="endnote|footnote">` nodes into "Notes"/"Footnotes" sections rendered ahead of the bibliography.

---

## Summary: exists vs. doesn't

**Exists**
- Two dossier routes (create, refine), form + conversational modes, AI drift report, start-over
- `BibEntry` as a full source model with provenance, target back-reference, and snippet
- A complete background research pipeline with live per-claim progress streaming
- Four pluggable research provider paths (BYOK search API, model web search, MCP, hosted Convex)
- Two near-duplicate bibliography UIs (`/apparatus/` route + `CitationsPanel` editor panel)
- Lix-blob-in-IndexedDB persistence with Convex sync (`bibliographyEntries` table)
- MLA/APA/Chicago formatters, dedupe by normalized URL, AI summarize, AI missing-claim detection
- A mature manuscript annotation system: comment / persona-note / suggestion marks, endnotes/footnotes, shared anchor-widget infrastructure
- MCP knowledge-base resource listing and reading

**Does not exist**
- Any "sources" view under `/dossier/` — the dossier is the brief, full stop
- Any canvas / graph / node / spatial UI, and **no library for one is installed** (d3/cytoscape are mermaid transitives only)
- Any annotation, note, highlight, or excerpt on a source (`BibEntry.note` is declared and entirely unused)
- Any durable link between a draft passage and a source — `target.anchor` is a fragile verbatim string; `isCited` is a URL string compare
- A citation mark/node in the editor schema; `citeInDraft` inserts inert plain text
- Any promotion flow for `accepted` (background entries are written `accepted: false` and stay that way)
- Any relationship *between* sources (no clustering, no grouping, no ordering beyond `provenance` split)
Exploration is done. Let me verify a few specifics in the actual code before I commit to an approach — particularly the framework constraint, since that rules out most canvas libraries.

# Source Canvas — a spatial board for the Apparatus and the dossier

## Context

Twyne's research lives in two flat lists. `/apparatus/` renders `BibEntry[]` as a two-column
list ("Found by the agents" | "Your bibliography"); `/dossier/refine/` renders the brief as a
vertical form with `DossierAttachment[]` in a separate editor. Neither shows **relationships** —
between sources, or between a source and the passage it was found for.

The linkage that exists today is deliberately thin and fragile:

- `BibEntry.target.anchor` is a verbatim ≤200-char copy of the draft passage. Edit the sentence and the association silently dies.
- `isCited` is a trailing-slash-normalized URL string compare against regex-detected URLs in the draft.
- `citeInDraft` inserts inert plain text — no mark, no id, nothing to walk back from.
- `BibEntry.note`, `citationKey`, `pageHint`, and `accepted` are declared on the interface and **never read or written by any UI**.

There is also no way to see *inside* a source. A `BibEntry` carries at most a ~600-char `snippet`.

We want the arky-style board from the reference: sources broken into structured excerpt cards laid
out in columns, arrows showing how they connect, a pinned reference panel on the right, and the
model annotating each card with how it bears on what the writer has actually written.

**Decisions taken** (from the user):
1. **Multiple excerpt cards per source** — fetch each source's text and split it into sectioned cards.
2. **Dossier board holds everything** — brief answers + attachments + every `BibEntry`, so the writer sees how the whole research picture fits together.
3. **Toggle, not replacement** — `/apparatus/` keeps its list and gains a `List | Canvas` switcher.

**The key enabling discovery:** `api.research.fetchSource({ url }) -> { title, author, …, markdown, embeddable }`
already exists at `convex/research.ts:350`, is rate-limited and provider-backed (TinyFish/Exa/Tavily),
and **has zero client callers**. `src/routes/apparatus/index.tsx:314` even has the `embedMarkdown`
state wired with the comment *"For now we show the iframe."* The extraction pipeline does not need a
new backend — it needs to call the action that is already there.

**Framework constraint:** this app is Qwik, not React. `react-flow`/`xyflow`/`tldraw`/`excalidraw`
are all React-only and would drag in `@builder.io/qwik-react`. Nothing spatial is installed
(`d3`/`cytoscape` in `bun.lock` are `mermaid@11` transitives — not a supported API surface).
**The canvas is hand-rolled with CSS transforms and one SVG layer. No new dependency.**

---

## Phase 1 — Data model and persistence

### New: `src/utils/source-canvas.ts`

Mirror `src/utils/bibliography.ts` exactly — it is the proven pattern for per-folio Lix-backed state.

```ts
const CANVAS_PATH = "/source-canvas.json";
export async function loadSourceCanvas(): Promise<SourceCanvas | null>   // readFileAsJson
export async function saveSourceCanvas(c: SourceCanvas): Promise<void>   // writeFileAsJson
export async function upsertNode(n: CanvasNode): Promise<SourceCanvas>
export async function deleteNode(id: string): Promise<SourceCanvas>      // cascades to child excerpts + incident edges
```

Types go in `src/types/index.ts` beside `BibEntry`/`ResearchTarget`:

```ts
export type CanvasNodeKind = "source" | "excerpt" | "brief" | "attachment" | "note";
export type EdgeKind = "supports" | "complicates" | "contradicts" | "extends" | "same-topic" | "manual";

export interface CanvasNode {
  id: string; folioId: string; kind: CanvasNodeKind;
  x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number;

  sourceId?: string;      // BibEntry.id — set on "source" and on every "excerpt"
  parentId?: string;      // excerpt -> its source node
  attachmentId?: string;  // DossierAttachment.id
  briefField?: string;    // ProjectBrief.answers key

  title: string;
  body?: string;          // excerpt markdown
  order?: number;         // excerpt order within its source (document order)

  annotation?: {
    relevance: string;                 // how this bears on the draft, in prose
    draftAnchor?: string;              // verbatim draft passage (same fragility as target.anchor — accepted)
    stance?: "supports" | "complicates" | "contradicts" | "background";
    score?: number;                    // 1-5
  };

  cluster?: string;
  collapsed?: boolean;
  pinned?: boolean;       // writer dragged it — auto-layout must never move it
  createdAt: number;
}

export interface CanvasEdge {
  id: string; from: string; to: string; kind: EdgeKind;
  label?: string; origin: "model" | "writer";
}

export interface SourceCanvas {
  version: 1; folioId: string;
  nodes: CanvasNode[]; edges: CanvasEdge[];
  clusters: { id: string; label: string; hue?: number }[];
  viewport: { x: number; y: number; zoom: number };
  lastMappedAt?: number;
}
```

### Sync

Register `/source-canvas.json` in `src/utils/convex-sync.ts` alongside `BIBLIOGRAPHY_PATH`
(declared `:227`, dirty-tracked `:758-786`, merged `:1289-1294`). Add a `sourceCanvas` row-per-node
collection in `convex/schema.ts` using the shared `collectionEntry` shape already used by
`bibliographyEntries` (`convex/schema.ts:45`), so a node-level edit doesn't rewrite the whole board.

**Rule: the canvas is a projection, never the store of record.** `BibEntry[]` stays authoritative for
sources; `ProjectBrief` stays authoritative for the brief. A canvas node holds only *layout +
annotation* and points at its owner by id. Deleting a `BibEntry` prunes its nodes on next load; a
node whose owner vanished is dropped, never resurrected.

---

## Phase 2 — Extraction pipeline

### New: `src/utils/source-extract.ts`

```ts
export async function extractSource(
  entry: BibEntry, settings: AiSettings,
): Promise<ExcerptCard[] | null>
```

1. **Get text.** `convexClient.action(api.research.fetchSource, { url: entry.url })` → `{ markdown, provider }`.
   Call it exactly the way `background-research.ts:543` calls `api.research.searchSources`.
   For a `DossierAttachment` with `kind: "document"` and a populated `.text`, skip the fetch entirely.
2. **Cache.** Write the raw markdown to `/source-text/<entryId>.md` in the Lix blob. Re-extraction and
   the embed overlay both read the cache; the network is hit once per source.
3. **Split.** `runClientSourceExtract(markdown, entry)` → `ExcerptCard[]` of
   `{ heading, body, order, kind: "section" | "figure" | "table" | "quote" }`, preserving document order.

**Cost guard — extraction is never automatic.** Each source card gets a `⌗ break out` action, plus one
`Extract all` batch button with an explicit source count and a confirm. This is the opposite of
`background-research.ts`'s debounced auto-fire, and deliberately so: that pipeline spends one cheap
search per pass, this one spends a fetch plus a long-context completion per source.
`MAX_EXTRACT_CHARS` caps markdown fed to the model; overflow splits across calls by heading.

### New AI features

Add `"source-extract"` and `"source-map"` to the `AiFeature` union (`src/types/index.ts:808`) and to
`defaultTemperature` (`src/utils/ai-client.ts:500`) — `0.1` and `0.3` respectively.

Four new prompt files in `prompts/` (loaded by basename via `import.meta.glob`, registered in
`src/utils/prompts.ts`):

| File | Job |
|---|---|
| `source-extract-system.md` / `-user.md` | Markdown → ordered excerpt cards. JSON only. Preserve the source's own headings; never invent content. |
| `source-map-system.md` / `-user.md` | Nodes + draft + brief → per-node annotation, cluster assignment, edge list. JSON only. |

Both `runClientSourceExtract` and `runClientSourceMap` go in `src/utils/ai-client.ts` following
`runClientSourceSummarize` (`:2124`) line for line: `resolveFeatureConfig` → `createModel` →
`renderNamed` → `generateTrackedText` (with `spanName` for the Arize span) → `stripReasoningTags` →
`JSON.parse` → defensive per-field filter that drops malformed rows instead of throwing.

---

## Phase 3 — The mapping pass

`runClientSourceMap` is the "model goes over it and relates it to what you've been writing" step.

**Input:** every node (title + trimmed body), the current draft text (from the `twyne:content` event
that `background-research.ts` already consumes), and the `ProjectBrief` answers.

**Output, applied to the board:**
- `annotation` per node — stance, 1-5 score, prose on how it bears on the draft, and a `draftAnchor` quote.
- `clusters` — 3-7 themes with labels, each node assigned one.
- `edges` — typed relations *between* nodes, each with a short label.

Triggered by an explicit `✦ Map connections` button showing node count and last-run time. Never on a
timer. Re-running preserves `pinned` positions and any `origin: "writer"` edge.

---

## Phase 4 — Canvas engine (`src/components/canvas/`)

No dependency. Qwik `component$` + Tailwind + `useStylesScoped$`, matching the hand-rolled style of
`src/routes/apparatus/index.tsx`.

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `source-canvas.tsx` | Host. Viewport state; pan by pointer-drag on background; zoom by wheel (clamp `0.15`–`2`); `transform: translate(…) scale(…)` on one stage div; zoom-% readout bottom-right as in the reference. |
| `canvas-card.tsx` | One node. Pointer-drag to move (sets `pinned: true`); collapse toggle; stance-tinted left border; excerpt cards visually nested under their source. |
| `canvas-edges.tsx` | Single absolutely-positioned SVG under the cards. Bezier paths between edge anchor points, arrowheads, dashes/color by `EdgeKind`. |
| `canvas-inspector.tsx` | The pinned `REFERENCE` panel from the reference image. Selected node: full excerpt body, the model's annotation, its `draftAnchor`, `⌖ open source`, `cite in draft`. |
| `../../utils/canvas-layout.ts` | Deterministic layout. Pure function, unit-testable. |

**Layout is column-packing, not a force simulation.** The reference image is columns — one per
cluster, excerpts stacked in `order` beneath their source, wrapping at a max column height. Columns
are deterministic (same input → same board), debuggable, and cheap. `pinned` nodes are treated as
fixed obstacles and never moved.

**Performance:** cards are plain DOM. Cull to nodes intersecting the viewport (plus a margin) once a
board exceeds ~150 nodes; below that, render all. Edge paths recompute only on drag-end, not per
pointermove.

---

## Phase 5 — Hosts

**`/apparatus/` (`src/routes/apparatus/index.tsx`)** — add `store.viewMode: "list" | "canvas"` and a
switcher reusing the existing `.style-toggle` scoped-CSS pattern. The current two-column grid
(`:747`) renders under `"list"`; `<SourceCanvas>` under `"canvas"`. Nothing existing is removed.

**`/dossier/refine/` (`src/routes/dossier/refine/index.tsx`)** — the same `<SourceCanvas>`, seeded
with brief-answer nodes, attachment nodes, and source nodes, so the writer sees premise and evidence
on one board. Sits alongside the existing form/conversational modes and the drift report.

**Seeding** (`seedCanvasFromFolio`, in `source-canvas.ts`): create a node for any `BibEntry`,
`DossierAttachment`, or non-empty brief answer that lacks one; drop nodes whose owner is gone; leave
every existing node's position untouched. Idempotent — safe to run on every mount.

---

## Deliberately out of scope

- **A citation mark in the ProseMirror schema.** The right fix for the fragile `draftAnchor` string is
  a real citation mark with an entry id, anchored by the existing `mark-anchor-widgets.ts` plugin.
  That is a schema migration touching export, exchange, and sync — its own piece of work. This plan
  matches today's `target.anchor` fidelity and no more.
- **PDF upload/parsing.** The reference video is PDF→canvas, but nothing in Twyne ingests a PDF today.
  Extraction here goes through `fetchSource`'s markdown. A PDF path is a clean later addition at the
  same `extractSource` seam.
- **Promoting `accepted`.** Still unused; not this change.

---

## Verification

1. `bun run build.types` — clean `tsc --noEmit`.
2. **Unit tests** (`bun test <file>` individually — the full suite has known cross-file interference):
   - `src/utils/canvas-layout.test.ts` — determinism (same input → identical output), `pinned` nodes never move, excerpts stay in `order` under their parent, no card overlap.
   - `src/utils/source-canvas.test.ts` — round-trip through `readFileAsJson`/`writeFileAsJson`; `seedCanvasFromFolio` idempotency; orphan pruning; delete-cascades-to-edges.
   - `src/utils/source-extract.test.ts` — malformed-JSON model output yields `null` rather than throwing; `MAX_EXTRACT_CHARS` overflow splits on headings.
   - `src/utils/ai-client.test.ts` — extend with `source-extract`/`source-map` cases in the style of the existing `source-summarize` case at `:43`.
3. **End-to-end, in the real app** (`/run`):
   - Open a folio with existing background sources → `/apparatus/` → toggle to Canvas → confirm one card per `BibEntry` with no mapping pass yet.
   - `⌗ break out` on one source → confirm `api.research.fetchSource` fires once (Network tab), excerpt cards appear in document order, and a second click serves from the Lix cache with no network call.
   - `✦ Map connections` → confirm clusters, arrows, and per-card annotations referencing actual draft passages.
   - Drag a card, reload the page → position persisted. Re-run mapping → dragged card has not moved.

# Source Canvas — a spatial board for the Apparatus and the dossier

## Context

Twyne's research lives in two flat lists. `/apparatus/` renders `BibEntry[]` as a two-column
list ("Found by the agents" | "Your bibliography"); `/dossier/refine/` renders the brief as a
vertical form with `DossierAttachment[]` in a separate editor. Neither shows **relationships** —
between sources, or between a source and the passage it was found for.

The linkage that exists today is deliberately thin and fragile:

- `BibEntry.target.anchor` is a verbatim ≤200-char copy of the draft passage. Edit the sentence and the association silently dies.
- `isCited` is a trailing-slash-normalized URL string compare against regex-detected URLs in the draft.
- `citeInDraft` inserts inert plain text — no mark, no id, nothing to walk back from.
- `BibEntry.note`, `citationKey`, `pageHint`, and `accepted` are declared on the interface and **never read or written by any UI**.

There is also no way to see *inside* a source. A `BibEntry` carries at most a ~600-char `snippet`.

We want the arky-style board from the reference: sources broken into structured excerpt cards laid
out in columns, arrows showing how they connect, a pinned reference panel on the right, and the
model annotating each card with how it bears on what the writer has actually written.

**Decisions taken** (from the user):
1. **Multiple excerpt cards per source** — fetch each source's text and split it into sectioned cards.
2. **Dossier board holds everything** — brief answers + attachments + every `BibEntry`, so the writer sees how the whole research picture fits together.
3. **Toggle, not replacement** — `/apparatus/` keeps its list and gains a `List | Canvas` switcher.

**The key enabling discovery:** `api.research.fetchSource({ url }) -> { title, author, …, markdown, embeddable }`
already exists at `convex/research.ts:350`, is rate-limited and provider-backed (TinyFish/Exa/Tavily),
and **has zero client callers**. `src/routes/apparatus/index.tsx:314` even has the `embedMarkdown`
state wired with the comment *"For now we show the iframe."* The extraction pipeline does not need a
new backend — it needs to call the action that is already there.

**Framework constraint:** this app is Qwik, not React. `react-flow`/`xyflow`/`tldraw`/`excalidraw`
are all React-only and would drag in `@builder.io/qwik-react`. Nothing spatial is installed
(`d3`/`cytoscape` in `bun.lock` are `mermaid@11` transitives — not a supported API surface).
**The canvas is hand-rolled with CSS transforms and one SVG layer. No new dependency.**

---

Mirror `src/utils/bibliography.ts` exactly — it is the proven pattern for per-folio Lix-backed state.

```ts
export async function saveSourceCanvas(c: SourceCanvas): Promise<void>   // writeFileAsJson
export async function upsertNode(n: CanvasNode): Promise<SourceCanvas>
export async function deleteNode(id: string): Promise<SourceCanvas>      // cascades to child excerpts + incident edges
```

```ts
export type CanvasNodeKind = "source" | "excerpt" | "brief" | "attachment" | "note";
export type EdgeKind = "supports" | "complicates" | "contradicts" | "extends" | "same-topic" | "manual";

export interface CanvasNode {
  id: string; folioId: string; kind: CanvasNodeKind;
  x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number;

  sourceId?: string;      // BibEntry.id — set on "source" and on every "excerpt"
  parentId?: string;      // excerpt -> its source node
  attachmentId?: string;  // DossierAttachment.id
  briefField?: string;    // ProjectBrief.answers key

  title: string;
  body?: string;          // excerpt markdown
  order?: number;         // excerpt order within its source (document order)

  annotation?: {
    relevance: string;                 // how this bears on the draft, in prose
    draftAnchor?: string;              // verbatim draft passage (same fragility as target.anchor — accepted)
    stance?: "supports" | "complicates" | "contradicts" | "background";
    score?: number;                    // 1-5
  };

  cluster?: string;
  collapsed?: boolean;
  pinned?: boolean;       // writer dragged it — auto-layout must never move it
  createdAt: number;
}

export interface CanvasEdge {
  id: string; from: string; to: string; kind: EdgeKind;
  label?: string; origin: "model" | "writer";
}

export interface SourceCanvas {
  version: 1; folioId: string;
  nodes: CanvasNode[]; edges: CanvasEdge[];
  clusters: { id: string; label: string; hue?: number }[];
  viewport: { x: number; y: number; zoom: number };
```

Register `/source-canvas.json` in `src/utils/convex-sync.ts` alongside `BIBLIOGRAPHY_PATH`

node whose owner vanished is dropped, never resurrected.

### New: `src/utils/source-extract.ts`

```ts
export async function extractSource(
  entry: BibEntry, settings: AiSettings,
): Promise<ExcerptCard[] | null>
```

2. **Cache.** Write the raw markdown to `/source-text/<entryId>.md` in the Lix blob. Re-extraction and

3. **Split.** `runClientSourceExtract(markdown, entry)` → `ExcerptCard[]` of

| File | Job |
|---|---|
| `source-extract-system.md` / `-user.md` | Markdown → ordered excerpt cards. JSON only. Preserve the source's own headings; never invent content. |
| `source-map-system.md` / `-user.md` | Nodes + draft + brief → per-node annotation, cluster assignment, edge list. JSON only. |

`renderNamed` → `generateTrackedText` (with `spanName` for the Arize span) → `stripReasoningTags` →
`JSON.parse` → defensive per-field filter that drops malformed rows instead of throwing.

---

## Phase 3 — The mapping pass

`runClientSourceMap` is the "model goes over it and relates it to what you've been writing" step.

**Input:** every node (title + trimmed body), the current draft text (from the `twyne:content` event
that `background-research.ts` already consumes), and the `ProjectBrief` answers.

**Output, applied to the board:**
- `annotation` per node — stance, 1-5 score, prose on how it bears on the draft, and a `draftAnchor` quote.
- `clusters` — 3-7 themes with labels, each node assigned one.
- `edges` — typed relations *between* nodes, each with a short label.

Triggered by an explicit `✦ Map connections` button showing node count and last-run time. Never on a
timer. Re-running preserves `pinned` positions and any `origin: "writer"` edge.

---

## Phase 4 — Canvas engine (`src/components/canvas/`)

No dependency. Qwik `component$` + Tailwind + `useStylesScoped$`, matching the hand-rolled style of
`src/routes/apparatus/index.tsx`.

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `source-canvas.tsx` | Host. Viewport state; pan by pointer-drag on background; zoom by wheel (clamp `0.15`–`2`); `transform: translate(…) scale(…)` on one stage div; zoom-% readout bottom-right as in the reference. |
| `canvas-card.tsx` | One node. Pointer-drag to move (sets `pinned: true`); collapse toggle; stance-tinted left border; excerpt cards visually nested under their source. |
| `canvas-edges.tsx` | Single absolutely-positioned SVG under the cards. Bezier paths between edge anchor points, arrowheads, dashes/color by `EdgeKind`. |
| `canvas-inspector.tsx` | The pinned `REFERENCE` panel from the reference image. Selected node: full excerpt body, the model's annotation, its `draftAnchor`, `⌖ open source`, `cite in draft`. |
| `../../utils/canvas-layout.ts` | Deterministic layout. Pure function, unit-testable. |

**Layout is column-packing, not a force simulation.** The reference image is columns — one per
cluster, excerpts stacked in `order` beneath their source, wrapping at a max column height. Columns

fixed obstacles and never moved.

**Performance:** cards are plain DOM. Cull to nodes intersecting the viewport (plus a margin) once a

pointermove.

OpenUI, from Thesys, is positioned as an "Open Standard for Generative UI" — an open-source toolkit whose stated purpose is "to make your AI agents respond with your UI." Instead of an agent replying with plain text or raw JSON that you then have to render yourself, the model composes an interface out of components you provide.

- Lets LLM agents emit UI descriptions in a dedicated spec ("OpenUI Lang"), rendered by an "OpenUI Runtime" in your app surface.
- Explicitly streaming-oriented: "UI renders progressively as the model responds, not after the full output."
- Interfaces are live rather than static — they "query your tools and MCP servers at runtime," with "Reactive state, inputs, and actions wired straight to your tools."
- Safety posture: "The model only composes your components and never runs arbitrary code."
- You supply your own component library: "Build from the components and design system you already have."

**Packaging and install**
It's distributed on the npm ecosystem, so JavaScript/TypeScript. The scaffolding command shown is:

```
pnpx @openuidev/cli@latest create
```

with bunx / yarn dlx / npx equivalents also listed. So the visible package is the CLI, `@openuidev/cli`. The page doesn't publish a runtime package name or any code-level API surface — no components, hooks, or function signatures appear.

**Framework targeting**
Not React-only. The claim is that "One spec renders natively to React, React Native, Vue, and more," which makes it framework-agnostic by design with per-framework renderers. Compatibility is advertised across three axes: any LLM (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek), any UI library (its own design system plus ShadCN, Material, DaisyUI, Base UI), and any agent framework (Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI and Anthropic Agents SDKs). It's also noted to work alongside CopilotKit and Assistant UI.

**Performance claim**
Benchmarked against JSON-based rendering, it claims to render "3x faster" using "67% fewer tokens" — with a benchmarks page linked for the methodology.

There's a hosted tier, OpenUI Cloud, adding report/slide generation with PPTX and PDF export, output validation to "Detect and correct invalid model output before it turns into broken UI," provider fallbacks and version pinning, pre-tested responsive components, design-token theming, and observability (latency percentiles, error frequency, audit trail).

One caveat worth flagging: this name collides with a separate, unrelated project also called "openui" (wandb's HTML/CSS generator), so verify you're pulling the Thesys one.

input.content:
# Source Canvas — a streaming, model-composed board for the Apparatus and the dossier

## Context

Twyne's research lives in two flat lists. `/apparatus/` renders `BibEntry[]` as a two-column list
("Found by the agents" | "Your bibliography"); `/dossier/refine/` renders the brief as a vertical form
with `DossierAttachment[]` in a separate editor. Neither shows **relationships** — between sources, or
between a source and the passage it was found for.

The linkage that exists today is deliberately thin and fragile:

- `BibEntry.target.anchor` is a verbatim ≤200-char copy of the draft passage. Edit the sentence and the association silently dies.
- `isCited` is a trailing-slash-normalized URL string compare against regex-detected URLs in the draft.
- `citeInDraft` inserts inert plain text — no mark, no id, nothing to walk back from.
- `BibEntry.note`, `citationKey`, `pageHint`, and `accepted` are declared on the interface and **never read or written by any UI**.

There is also no way to see *inside* a source. A `BibEntry` carries at most a ~600-char `snippet`.

We want the arky-style board from the reference: sources broken into structured cards laid out in
columns, arrows showing how they connect, a pinned reference panel on the right, and the model
annotating each card with how it bears on what the writer has actually written.

### Decisions taken

1. **Multiple excerpt cards per source** — fetch each source's text and split it into sectioned cards.
2. **Dossier board holds everything** — brief answers + attachments + every `BibEntry` on one board.
3. **Toggle, not replacement** — `/apparatus/` keeps its list and gains a `List | Canvas` switcher.
4. **Automatic, not on-demand** — extraction fires on its own, like `background-research.ts` does.
5. **Streaming, rendered through OpenUI** — cards paint progressively as the model composes them.
6. **Resizable** — the board and its reference panel can be pulled larger.

### Two enabling discoveries

**`fetchSource` already exists.** `api.research.fetchSource({ url }) -> { title, author, …, markdown, embeddable }`
sits at `convex/research.ts:350`, rate-limited and provider-backed (TinyFish/Exa/Tavily), with **zero
client callers**. `src/routes/apparatus/index.tsx:314` even has `embedMarkdown` state wired next to the
comment *"For now we show the iframe."* Extraction needs no new backend.

**OpenUI has a framework-agnostic core.** Twyne is Qwik, and OpenUI ships renderers only for React,
Vue, and Svelte — **there is no Qwik renderer**. But `@openuidev/lang-core@0.2.11` is exactly what its
description says: *"Framework-agnostic core for OpenUI Lang: parser, prompt generation, validation, and
type definitions."* Its verified exports include `createStreamingParser`, `parse`, `defineComponent`,
`createLibrary`, `generateSystemPrompt`, `createStore`, `createQueryManager`, `evaluate`, `validate`,
and the `ASTNode` / `ElementNode` / `StreamParser` / `ComponentRenderProps` types.

It has **zero runtime dependencies**. Its two peers are already installed at compatible versions:
`zod@^4.4.3` (wants `^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0`) and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30.0` (wants `>=1.0.0`).
**Adding it pulls in no new transitive dependencies.**

The framework packages are thin. `@openuidev/svelte-lang@0.1.2` depends on nothing but `lang-core` and
ships six source files — `Renderer.svelte`, `RenderNode.svelte`, `context.svelte.js`, `library.js`,
`validation.svelte.js`, `index.js`. **A Qwik renderer is the same shape: a recursive node walker, a host,
a context, and a library helper.** The core does the hard part (streaming XML-DSL parse with partial
tags, validation, system-prompt generation); we supply the Qwik mapping.

### Why OpenUI is the right fit here, not overkill

For a fixed schema (`heading`, `body`, `order`), OpenUI would be heavier than `streamObject`. But look
at what the reference board actually contains: tables, flowcharts, nested bullet hierarchies, figures,
comparison matrices, callouts. **The cards are heterogeneous, and the model chooses which shape fits each
chunk of a source.** That is precisely OpenUI's use case — the model composes from *our* component
library and never runs arbitrary code. `generateSystemPrompt(library)` also replaces a hand-written
extraction prompt: the components define the contract.

**Canvas geometry stays ours.** OpenUI composes *card interiors*. Node positions, edges, clustering, pan,
and zoom are Twyne's own state in `/source-canvas.json` — never model-authored layout.

---

## Phase 1 — Data model and persistence

### New: `src/utils/source-canvas.ts`

Mirror `src/utils/bibliography.ts` — the proven pattern for per-folio Lix-backed state.

```ts
const CANVAS_PATH = "/source-canvas.json";
export async function loadSourceCanvas(): Promise<SourceCanvas | null>   // readFileAsJson
export async function saveSourceCanvas(c: SourceCanvas): Promise<void>   // writeFileAsJson
export async function upsertNode(n: CanvasNode): Promise<SourceCanvas>
export async function deleteNode(id: string): Promise<SourceCanvas>      // cascades to child cards + incident edges
```

Types go in `src/types/index.ts` beside `BibEntry` / `ResearchTarget`:

```ts
export type CanvasNodeKind = "source" | "excerpt" | "brief" | "attachment" | "note";
export type EdgeKind = "supports" | "complicates" | "contradicts" | "extends" | "same-topic" | "manual";

export interface CanvasNode {
  id: string; folioId: string; kind: CanvasNodeKind;
  x: number; y: number; w: number; h: number;

  sourceId?: string;      // BibEntry.id — set on "source" and on every "excerpt"
  parentId?: string;      // excerpt -> its source node
  attachmentId?: string;  // DossierAttachment.id
  briefField?: string;    // ProjectBrief.answers key

  title: string;
  ouiLang?: string;       // OpenUI Lang source for this card's interior
  order?: number;         // document order within its source

  annotation?: {
    relevance: string;                 // how this bears on the draft, in prose
    draftAnchor?: string;              // verbatim draft passage (same fragility as target.anchor — accepted)
    stance?: "supports" | "complicates" | "contradicts" | "background";
    score?: number;                    // 1-5
  };

  cluster?: string;
  collapsed?: boolean;
  pinned?: boolean;       // writer dragged or resized it — auto-layout must never move it
  streaming?: boolean;    // card is mid-compose; renderer shows partial AST
  createdAt: number;
}

export interface CanvasEdge {
  id: string; from: string; to: string; kind: EdgeKind;
  label?: string; origin: "model" | "writer";
}

export interface SourceCanvas {
  version: 1; folioId: string;
  nodes: CanvasNode[]; edges: CanvasEdge[];
  clusters: { id: string; label: string; hue?: number }[];
  viewport: { x: number; y: number; zoom: number };
  inspectorWidth: number; expanded: boolean;
  lastMappedAt?: number;
}
```

### Sync

Register `/source-canvas.json` in `src/utils/convex-sync.ts` alongside `BIBLIOGRAPHY_PATH` (declared
`:227`, dirty-tracked `:758-786`, merged `:1289-1294`). Add a `sourceCanvas` row-per-node collection in
`convex/schema.ts` using the shared `collectionEntry` shape already used by `bibliographyEntries`
(`convex/schema.ts:45`), so a node-level edit doesn't rewrite the whole board.

**Rule: the canvas is a projection, never the store of record.** `BibEntry[]` stays authoritative for
sources; `ProjectBrief` stays authoritative for the brief. A node holds only *layout + annotation +
composed interior* and points at its owner by id. A node whose owner vanished is dropped, never
resurrected. **Never persist while `streaming: true`** — only completed cards are written, so a mid-stream
reload can't strand a half-parsed AST in the Lix blob.

---

## Phase 2 — OpenUI component library and Qwik renderer

### `bun add @openuidev/lang-core`

### New: `src/components/canvas/openui/` — the Qwik renderer

Modelled on `@openuidev/svelte-lang`'s six-file shape.

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `library.ts` | `defineComponent` for each Twyne card primitive; `createLibrary` assembles them. The single source of truth for what the model may emit. |
| `render-node.tsx` | Recursive `ASTNode` → Qwik walker. Handles `ElementNode`, text, and the **partial/unterminated nodes** the streaming parser emits. |
| `renderer.tsx` | Host. Owns the `createStore` instance, wires `createQueryManager` to our MCP tools, renders the root. |
| `context.ts` | Qwik `createContextId` for store + library, so `render-node` needn't thread props. |
| `stream.ts` | Wraps `createStreamingParser`; feeds model deltas in, emits AST snapshots out. Reuses the `createPublishGate` batching already in `src/utils/generation-stream.ts:238` so re-renders are coalesced rather than one-per-token. |

### The component library — what the model composes with

`Section`, `KeyValueTable`, `Flow`, `Quote`, `Figure`, `Comparison`, `Callout`, `BulletTree`, `Annotation`.
Each `defineComponent` carries a zod prop schema and a description; `generateSystemPrompt(library)` turns
them into the extraction system prompt. Every one renders in Twyne's existing letterpress idiom
(Tailwind + CSS variables + `useStylesScoped$`), matching `src/routes/apparatus/index.tsx`.

**This replaces a hand-written `source-extract-system.md`.** Adding a card shape means adding a component,
not editing a prompt.

---

## Phase 3 — Automatic streaming extraction

### New: `src/utils/source-extract.ts`

```ts
export function onSourcesChanged(entries: BibEntry[]): void   // debounced watcher
export async function extractSource(entry: BibEntry, settings: AiSettings): Promise<void>
```

Per source:

1. **Get text.** `convexClient.action(api.research.fetchSource, { url: entry.url })` → `{ markdown, provider }`,
   called the way `background-research.ts:543` calls `api.research.searchSources`. A `DossierAttachment`
   with `kind: "document"` and populated `.text` skips the fetch entirely.
2. **Cache.** Raw markdown → `/source-text/<entryId>.md` in the Lix blob. Re-extraction and the embed
   overlay read the cache; the network is hit once per source, ever.
3. **Stream-compose.** `generateTrackedText`'s streaming sibling feeds deltas into `stream.ts`'s parser.
   Each completed top-level element becomes a `CanvasNode` with `streaming: true`, laid out immediately and
   painted as it fills in. On finish, `streaming: false` and the board persists.

### Automatic, with the same guardrails the existing watcher uses

This mirrors `background-research.ts` deliberately — same shape, same safety valves:

- Fires on the `twyne:background-sources` event that already announces a landed source, plus on folio switch.
- `DEBOUNCE_MS` window so a burst of finds is one pass.
- `MAX_EXTRACT_PER_PASS = 2` and a per-folio ceiling matching `MAX_BACKGROUND_PER_FOLIO = 25`.
- Skips any source already cached; a failed fetch is marked and not retried in the same session.
- Honors the existing `apparatusSettings` gate, so it can be switched off.

*One flag, then it's your call:* unlike the search pass this spends a fetch **plus** a long-context
completion per source, so a 25-source folio is ~25 such calls on first run. The caps and the cache mean
that cost is paid once and never on a timer — but it is real, and worth watching on the hosted path.

### Progressive layout

A card that is still streaming must not make the board jump. `canvas-layout.ts` reserves each streaming
node's slot at its declared `w`/`h` and reflows only on stream completion.

---

## Phase 4 — Canvas engine (`src/components/canvas/`)

No spatial dependency. Qwik `component$` + Tailwind + `useStylesScoped$`, matching the hand-rolled style
of `src/routes/apparatus/index.tsx`. (react-flow / xyflow / tldraw / excalidraw are all React-only and
would drag in `@builder.io/qwik-react`. `d3` and `cytoscape` in `bun.lock` are `mermaid@11` transitives,
not a usable API surface.)

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `source-canvas.tsx` | Host. Viewport state; pan by pointer-drag on background; zoom by wheel (clamp `0.15`–`2`); `transform: translate(…) scale(…)` on one stage div; zoom-% readout bottom-right as in the reference. |
| `canvas-card.tsx` | One node. Drag to move; **corner handle to resize** (both set `pinned: true`); collapse toggle; stance-tinted left border; interior rendered by the OpenUI renderer; skeleton shimmer while `streaming`. |
| `canvas-edges.tsx` | Single absolutely-positioned SVG under the cards. Bezier paths, arrowheads, dash/color by `EdgeKind`. |
| `canvas-inspector.tsx` | The pinned `REFERENCE` panel from the reference image. Selected node: full interior, the model's annotation, its `draftAnchor`, `⌖ open source`, `cite in draft`. |
| `../../utils/canvas-layout.ts` | Deterministic column packing. Pure, unit-testable. |

### Pulling the view larger

Three levers, all reusing patterns already in the repo:

- **Inspector width** — drag handle cloned from `src/routes/editor/index.tsx:1418-1445`: `w-1.5 cursor-col-resize`, `mousedown` → `mousemove` with `Math.max/min` clamping → `mouseup` cleanup that restores `document.body.style.cursor`. Persists to `SourceCanvas.inspectorWidth`.
- **Expand the board** — a full-bleed toggle that hides the inspector and lets the stage take the viewport. Persists to `SourceCanvas.expanded`.
- **Resize a card** — corner handle writing `w`/`h`, with `pinned: true` so layout leaves it alone.

**Layout is column packing, not a force simulation.** The reference is columns — one per cluster, excerpts
stacked in `order` beneath their source, wrapping at a max column height. Deterministic (same input → same
board), debuggable, cheap. `pinned` nodes are fixed obstacles.

**Performance:** cards are plain DOM. Cull to nodes intersecting the viewport plus a margin once a board
exceeds ~150 nodes. Edge paths recompute on drag-end, not per `pointermove`.

---

## Phase 5 — The mapping pass and the hosts

### Mapping

`runClientSourceMap` in `src/utils/ai-client.ts`, following `runClientSourceSummarize` (`:2124`) line for
line: `resolveFeatureConfig` → `createModel` → `renderNamed` → `generateTrackedText` (with `spanName` for
the Arize span) → `stripReasoningTags` → parse → defensive per-field filter that drops malformed rows
rather than throwing.

Add `"source-map"` to the `AiFeature` union (`src/types/index.ts:808`) and `defaultTemperature`
(`src/utils/ai-client.ts:500`, use `0.3`), plus `prompts/source-map-system.md` and `-user.md` registered in
`src/utils/prompts.ts`. *(No `source-extract` prompt files — `generateSystemPrompt` covers that.)*

**Input:** every node, the draft text (from the `twyne:content` event `background-research.ts` already
consumes), and the `ProjectBrief`. **Output:** per-node `annotation`, 3–7 labelled `clusters`, and typed
`edges`. Runs after an extraction pass settles, and on an explicit `✦ Map connections` re-run. Re-running
preserves `pinned` positions and every `origin: "writer"` edge.

### Hosts

**`/apparatus/`** — add `store.viewMode: "list" | "canvas"` and a switcher reusing the existing
`.style-toggle` scoped-CSS pattern. The current two-column grid (`:747`) renders under `"list"`,
`<SourceCanvas>` under `"canvas"`. Nothing existing is removed.

**`/dossier/refine/`** — the same `<SourceCanvas>`, seeded with brief-answer, attachment, and source nodes,
alongside the existing form/conversational modes and the drift report.

**Seeding** (`seedCanvasFromFolio`): create a node for any `BibEntry`, `DossierAttachment`, or non-empty
brief answer lacking one; drop orphans; never touch an existing node's position. Idempotent — safe on
every mount.

---

## Deliberately out of scope

- **A citation mark in the ProseMirror schema.** The right fix for the fragile `draftAnchor` is a real mark
  carrying an entry id, anchored by the existing `mark-anchor-widgets.ts` plugin. That's a schema migration
  touching export, exchange, and sync — its own piece of work. This plan matches today's `target.anchor`
  fidelity and no more.
- **PDF ingestion.** The reference video is PDF→canvas; nothing in Twyne ingests a PDF today. Extraction
  goes through `fetchSource`'s markdown. A PDF path is a clean later addition at the `extractSource` seam.
- **Upstreaming the Qwik renderer** to `@openuidev/qwik-lang`. Worth doing once it's proven; not now.

---

## Verification

1. `bun run build.types` — clean `tsc --noEmit`.

# Source Canvas — a streaming, model-composed board for the Apparatus and the dossier

## Context

Twyne's research lives in two flat lists. `/apparatus/` renders `BibEntry[]` as a two-column list
("Found by the agents" | "Your bibliography"); `/dossier/refine/` renders the brief as a vertical form
with `DossierAttachment[]` in a separate editor. Neither shows **relationships** — between sources, or
between a source and the passage it was found for.

The linkage that exists today is deliberately thin and fragile:

- `BibEntry.target.anchor` is a verbatim ≤200-char copy of the draft passage. Edit the sentence and the association silently dies.
- `isCited` is a trailing-slash-normalized URL string compare against regex-detected URLs in the draft.
- `citeInDraft` inserts inert plain text — no mark, no id, nothing to walk back from.
- `BibEntry.note`, `citationKey`, `pageHint`, and `accepted` are declared on the interface and **never read or written by any UI**.

There is also no way to see *inside* a source. A `BibEntry` carries at most a ~600-char `snippet`.

We want the arky-style board from the reference: sources broken into structured cards laid out in
columns, arrows showing how they connect, a pinned reference panel on the right, and the model
annotating each card with how it bears on what the writer has actually written.

### Decisions taken

1. **Multiple excerpt cards per source** — fetch each source's text and split it into sectioned cards.
2. **Dossier board holds everything** — brief answers + attachments + every `BibEntry` on one board.
3. **Toggle, not replacement** — `/apparatus/` keeps its list and gains a `List | Canvas` switcher.
4. **Automatic, not on-demand** — extraction fires on its own, like `background-research.ts` does.
5. **Streaming, rendered through OpenUI** — cards paint progressively as the model composes them.
6. **Resizable** — the board and its reference panel can be pulled larger.

### Two enabling discoveries

**`fetchSource` already exists.** `api.research.fetchSource({ url }) -> { title, author, …, markdown, embeddable }`
sits at `convex/research.ts:350`, rate-limited and provider-backed (TinyFish/Exa/Tavily), with **zero
client callers**. `src/routes/apparatus/index.tsx:314` even has `embedMarkdown` state wired next to the
comment *"For now we show the iframe."* Extraction needs no new backend.

**OpenUI has a framework-agnostic core.** Twyne is Qwik, and OpenUI ships renderers only for React,
Vue, and Svelte — **there is no Qwik renderer**. But `@openuidev/lang-core@0.2.11` is exactly what its
description says: *"Framework-agnostic core for OpenUI Lang: parser, prompt generation, validation, and
type definitions."* Its verified exports include `createStreamingParser`, `parse`, `defineComponent`,
`createLibrary`, `generateSystemPrompt`, `createStore`, `createQueryManager`, `evaluate`, `validate`,
and the `ASTNode` / `ElementNode` / `StreamParser` / `ComponentRenderProps` types.

It has **zero runtime dependencies**. Its two peers are already installed at compatible versions:
`zod@^4.4.3` (wants `^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0`) and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@^1.30.0` (wants `>=1.0.0`).
**Adding it pulls in no new transitive dependencies.**

The framework packages are thin. `@openuidev/svelte-lang@0.1.2` depends on nothing but `lang-core` and
ships six source files — `Renderer.svelte`, `RenderNode.svelte`, `context.svelte.js`, `library.js`,
`validation.svelte.js`, `index.js`. **A Qwik renderer is the same shape: a recursive node walker, a host,
a context, and a library helper.** The core does the hard part (streaming XML-DSL parse with partial
tags, validation, system-prompt generation); we supply the Qwik mapping.

### Why OpenUI is the right fit here, not overkill

For a fixed schema (`heading`, `body`, `order`), OpenUI would be heavier than `streamObject`. But look
at what the reference board actually contains: tables, flowcharts, nested bullet hierarchies, figures,
comparison matrices, callouts. **The cards are heterogeneous, and the model chooses which shape fits each
chunk of a source.** That is precisely OpenUI's use case — the model composes from *our* component
library and never runs arbitrary code. `generateSystemPrompt(library)` also replaces a hand-written
extraction prompt: the components define the contract.

**Canvas geometry stays ours.** OpenUI composes *card interiors*. Node positions, edges, clustering, pan,
and zoom are Twyne's own state in `/source-canvas.json` — never model-authored layout.

---

## Phase 1 — Data model and persistence

### New: `src/utils/source-canvas.ts`

Mirror `src/utils/bibliography.ts` — the proven pattern for per-folio Lix-backed state.

```ts
  id: string; folioId: string; kind: CanvasNodeKind;

  parentId?: string;      // excerpt -> its source node
  attachmentId?: string;  // DossierAttachment.id
```

/**
 * The OpenUI component library — the contract between the model and the canvas.
 *
 * When a source is extracted, the model does not fill in a fixed schema. It
 * *composes* each card from the primitives below, choosing the shape that fits
 * the material: a definition list becomes a KeyValueTable, a cascade becomes a
 * Flow, a side-by-side becomes a Comparison. That is why this is OpenUI Lang
 * and not `streamObject` — the reference boards are heterogeneous, and the
 * model is the one who knows which shape a given passage wants.
 *
 * Two boundaries this file draws, both load-bearing:
 *
 *   1. **The model composes card interiors. It never authors canvas geometry.**
 *      No component here has an x, y, width, or z-index. Node positions, edges,
 *      clusters, pan, and zoom are Twyne's own state in `/source-canvas.json`.
 *
 *   2. **Transcription, not composition of new claims.** Every description below
 *      says so, because `library.prompt()` turns these descriptions into the
 *      extraction system prompt. There is no `source-extract-system.md` — adding
 *      a card shape means adding a component here, and the prompt follows.
 *
 * The renderer (`renderer.tsx` / `render-node.tsx`) walks the parsed AST and
 * calls the Qwik component in each definition's `component` slot. lang-core
 * never inspects that value; it is opaque to the parser and consumed only by
 * our adapter.
 */

import { z } from "zod";
import { createLibrary, defineComponent } from "@openuidev/lang-core";

import {
  AnnotationBlock,
  CalloutBlock,
  CardBlock,
  CardsRoot,
  ComparisonBlock,
  FigureBlock,
  FlowBlock,
  KeyValueTableBlock,
  OutlineBlock,
  ProseBlock,
  QuoteBlock,
} from "./primitives";

/**
 * Shared fidelity language. Repeated into the descriptions the model actually
 * reads rather than stated once, because the prompt generator emits each
 * component's description independently and a rule stated only at the top of
 * the library is a rule the model sees once and drifts from by card forty.
 */
const VERBATIM = "Use the source's own wording. Do not paraphrase or embellish.";

/* ── Leaf shapes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

export const Prose = defineComponent({
  name: "Prose",
  description:
    "A short run of plain explanatory text, one to four sentences. The fallback " +
    "when the passage has no other structure. " +
    VERBATIM +
    " Prefer Outline when the source uses numbering or bullets.",
  props: z.object({
    text: z.string().describe("The passage, as it appears in the source."),
  }),
  component: ProseBlock,
});

export const Outline = defineComponent({
  name: "Outline",
  description:
    "A hierarchical list: numbered sections, lettered sub-points, bullets. This " +
    "is the workhorse for reference material, which is mostly nested outlines. " +
    "Nesting is expressed by each item's `depth` rather than by containment, so " +
    "a deep list streams without waiting for closing brackets. " +
    VERBATIM +
    " Keep the source's own numbering inside the text (e.g. \"(1) Antithrombin III\").",
  props: z.object({
    items: z
      .array(
        z.object({
          text: z.string().describe("One line of the outline, numbering included."),
          depth: z
            .number()
            .int()
            .min(0)
            .max(4)
            .describe("Indent level. 0 is top level; each nesting step adds one."),
          emphasis: z
            .boolean()
            .optional()
            .describe("True if the source bolds or underlines this line."),
        }),
      )
      .describe("Lines in document order."),
  }),
  component: OutlineBlock,
});

export const KeyValueTable = defineComponent({
  name: "KeyValueTable",
  description:
    "A two-column definition table: a term on the left, its explanation on the " +
    "right. Use for glossaries, factor lists, property/description pairs, and " +
    "any 'X — what X does' layout. " +
    VERBATIM,
  props: z.object({
    caption: z.string().optional().describe("Table heading, if the source gives one."),
    rows: z
      .array(
        z.object({
          key: z.string().describe("The term, in the left column."),
          value: z.string().describe("Its explanation, in the right column."),
        }),
      )
      .describe("Rows in document order."),
  }),
  component: KeyValueTableBlock,
});

export const Comparison = defineComponent({
  name: "Comparison",
  description:
    "A matrix comparing two or more things across the same set of attributes — " +
    "the 'TTP vs. HUS' shape. Use when the source sets items side by side. Every " +
    "row must have one cell per column, in column order; use an empty string when " +
    "the source leaves a cell blank. " +
    VERBATIM,
  props: z.object({
    caption: z.string().optional().describe("What is being compared."),
    columns: z
      .array(z.string())
      .describe("The things being compared, e.g. [\"TTP\", \"Typical HUS\"]."),
    rows: z
      .array(
        z.object({
          label: z.string().describe("The attribute, e.g. \"Etiology\"."),
          cells: z
            .array(z.string())
            .describe("One value per column, in the same order as `columns`."),
        }),
      )
      .describe("Attribute rows in document order."),
  }),
  component: ComparisonBlock,
});

export const Flow = defineComponent({
  name: "Flow",
  description:
    "A process or decision tree: a cascade, a pathway, a diagnostic algorithm. " +
    "Steps are given as a flat list; a step that follows others names them in " +
    "`after`, which lets one list describe both a straight sequence and a " +
    "branching tree. Omit `after` on the entry step. " +
    VERBATIM,
  props: z.object({
    caption: z.string().optional().describe("What the flow depicts."),
    steps: z
      .array(
        z.object({
          id: z
            .string()
            .describe("Short stable handle for this step, referenced by `after`."),
          label: z.string().describe("The step, as the source names it."),
          detail: z.string().optional().describe("A clarifying clause, if the source gives one."),
          after: z
            .array(z.string())
            .optional()
            .describe("Ids of the steps this one follows. Omit for the entry step."),
        }),
      )
      .describe("Every step in the process."),
  }),
  component: FlowBlock,
});

export const Quote = defineComponent({
  name: "Quote",
  description:
    "A verbatim passage worth citing directly — the writer may quote it in the " +
    "draft, so it must be exact. Never trim, normalise, or fix the source's " +
    "wording. Include a page or section locator in `locator` when the source " +
    "shows one.",
  props: z.object({
    text: z.string().describe("The passage, character for character."),
    locator: z
      .string()
      .optional()
      .describe("Page, section, or timestamp, e.g. \"p. 412\" or \"§3.2\"."),
  }),
  component: QuoteBlock,
});

export const Figure = defineComponent({
  name: "Figure",
  description:
    "An image, diagram, or micrograph from the source. Only ever use a `src` URL " +
    "that appears in the source text — never invent, guess, or reconstruct an " +
    "image URL. When the source describes a figure you cannot link to, use " +
    "Callout with the description instead.",
  props: z.object({
    src: z.string().describe("Image URL exactly as it appears in the source."),
    alt: z.string().describe("What the figure shows, for screen readers."),
    caption: z.string().optional().describe("The source's own caption, if it has one."),
  }),
  component: FigureBlock,
});

export const Callout = defineComponent({
  name: "Callout",
  description:
    "A boxed aside the source itself sets apart: a warning, a contraindication, " +
    "a key takeaway, a note. Use `tone` to match how the source frames it. Do not " +
    "promote ordinary prose into a Callout for emphasis — reserve it for material " +
    "the source visually distinguishes.",
  props: z.object({
    tone: z
      .enum(["note", "warning", "key", "caveat"])
      .describe("How the source frames this aside."),
    title: z.string().optional().describe("The aside's own heading, if any."),
    text: z.string().describe("The aside's content."),
  }),
  component: CalloutBlock,
});

/**
 * The one component whose content the model authors rather than transcribes.
 * Kept deliberately separate from the transcription primitives, and rendered in
 * a visually distinct register, so the writer can always tell the source's voice
 * from the machine's.
 */
export const Annotation = defineComponent({
  name: "Annotation",
  description:
    "Your own note on how this card bears on the writer's draft — the single " +
    "place you may write rather than transcribe. Say what the card does for the " +
    "argument: what it supports, complicates, or contradicts. Quote the draft " +
    "passage you mean in `draftAnchor`, verbatim and short. At most one " +
    "Annotation per card, and only when you have something substantive; an " +
    "Annotation that restates the card is worse than none.",
  props: z.object({
    stance: z
      .enum(["supports", "complicates", "contradicts", "background"])
      .describe("How this card sits with what the draft currently claims."),
    relevance: z.string().describe("One or two sentences on why this matters here."),
    draftAnchor: z
      .string()
      .optional()
      .describe("The draft passage this speaks to, quoted verbatim, under 30 words."),
    score: z
      .number()
      .int()
      .min(1)
      .max(5)
      .optional()
      .describe("1–5: how much the writer should care right now. 5 is urgent."),
  }),
  component: AnnotationBlock,
});

/* ── Card and root ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

const BLOCK_REFS = [
  Prose.ref,
  Outline.ref,
  KeyValueTable.ref,
  Comparison.ref,
  Flow.ref,
  Quote.ref,
  Figure.ref,
  Callout.ref,
  Annotation.ref,
] as const;

export const Card = defineComponent({
  name: "Card",
  description:
    "One card on the canvas: a single coherent section of the source. Split a " +
    "source at its own section boundaries — a card should be one idea a reader " +
    "could take in at a glance, not a whole document and not a single sentence. " +
    "Give it the source's own section heading as `title`. Compose the interior " +
    "from whichever blocks fit the material; mixing them is normal and expected.",
  props: z.object({
    title: z.string().describe("The section heading, from the source where possible."),
    blocks: z.array(z.union([...BLOCK_REFS])).describe("The card's contents, in document order."),
  }),
  component: CardBlock,
});

export const Cards = defineComponent({
  name: "Cards",
  description:

 * The OpenUI component library — the contract between the model and the canvas.
 *
 * When a source is extracted, the model does not fill in a fixed schema. It
 * *composes* each card from the primitives below, choosing the shape that fits

 * and not `streamObject` — the reference boards are heterogeneous, and the
 * model is the one who knows which shape a given passage wants.
 *
 * Two boundaries this file draws, both load-bearing:
 *
 *   1. **The model composes card interiors. It never authors canvas geometry.**
 *      No component here has an x, y, width, or z-index. Node positions, edges,
 *      clusters, pan, and zoom are Twyne's own state in `/source-canvas.json`.
 *
 *   2. **Transcription, not composition of new claims.** Every description below
 *      says so, because `library.prompt()` turns these descriptions into the
 *      extraction system prompt. There is no `source-extract-system.md` — adding
 *      a card shape means adding a component here, and the prompt follows.
 *
 * The renderer (`renderer.tsx` / `render-node.tsx`) walks the parsed AST and
 * calls the Qwik component in each definition's `component` slot. lang-core
 * never inspects that value; it is opaque to the parser and consumed only by
 * our adapter.

  CardBlock,

  OutlineBlock,
  ProseBlock,
  QuoteBlock,

 * reads rather than stated once, because the prompt generator emits each
 * component's description independently and a rule stated only at the top of
 * the library is a rule the model sees once and drifts from by card forty.
 */

  name: "Prose",
  description:
    "A short run of plain explanatory text, one to four sentences. The fallback " +
    "when the passage has no other structure. " +
    VERBATIM +
    " Prefer Outline when the source uses numbering or bullets.",
  props: z.object({
    text: z.string().describe("The passage, as it appears in the source."),
  }),
  component: ProseBlock,
});

  name: "Outline",
  description:
    "A hierarchical list: numbered sections, lettered sub-points, bullets. This " +
    "is the workhorse for reference material, which is mostly nested outlines. " +
    "Nesting is expressed by each item's `depth` rather than by containment, so " +
    "a deep list streams without waiting for closing brackets. " +
    VERBATIM +
    " Keep the source's own numbering inside the text (e.g. \"(1) Antithrombin III\").",
  props: z.object({
    items: z
      .array(
        z.object({
          text: z.string().describe("One line of the outline, numbering included."),
          depth: z
            .number()
            .int()
            .min(0)
            .max(4)
            .describe("Indent level. 0 is top level; each nesting step adds one."),
          emphasis: z
            .boolean()
            .optional()
            .describe("True if the source bolds or underlines this line."),
        }),
      )
      .describe("Lines in document order."),
  }),
  component: OutlineBlock,
});

  name: "KeyValueTable",
  description:
    "A two-column definition table: a term on the left, its explanation on the " +
    "right. Use for glossaries, factor lists, property/description pairs, and " +
    "any 'X — what X does' layout. " +
    VERBATIM,
  props: z.object({
    caption: z.string().optional().describe("Table heading, if the source gives one."),
    rows: z
      .array(
        z.object({
          key: z.string().describe("The term, in the left column."),
          value: z.string().describe("Its explanation, in the right column."),
        }),
      )
      .describe("Rows in document order."),
  }),
  component: KeyValueTableBlock,
});

  name: "Comparison",
  description:

    "the 'TTP vs. HUS' shape. Use when the source sets items side by side. Every " +
    "row must have one cell per column, in column order; use an empty string when " +
    "the source leaves a cell blank. " +

  props: z.object({
    caption: z.string().optional().describe("What is being compared."),
    columns: z

    rows: z
      .array(

  }),
  component: ComparisonBlock,

    "branching tree. Omit `after` on the entry step. " +

  props: z.object({
    caption: z.string().optional().describe("What the flow depicts."),
    steps: z

          detail: z.string().optional().describe("A clarifying clause, if the source gives one."),

            .array(z.string())

            .describe("Ids of the steps this one follows. Omit for the entry step."),

  }),
  component: FlowBlock,
});

    "draft, so it must be exact. Never trim, normalise, or fix the source's " +
    "wording. Include a page or section locator in `locator` when the source " +
    "shows one.",
  props: z.object({
    text: z.string().describe("The passage, character for character."),
    locator: z
      .string()
      .optional()
      .describe("Page, section, or timestamp, e.g. \"p. 412\" or \"§3.2\"."),
  }),
  component: QuoteBlock,
});

  name: "Figure",
  description:
    "An image, diagram, or micrograph from the source. Only ever use a `src` URL " +
    "that appears in the source text — never invent, guess, or reconstruct an " +
    "image URL. When the source describes a figure you cannot link to, use " +
    "Callout with the description instead.",
  props: z.object({
    src: z.string().describe("Image URL exactly as it appears in the source."),
    alt: z.string().describe("What the figure shows, for screen readers."),
    caption: z.string().optional().describe("The source's own caption, if it has one."),
  }),
  component: FigureBlock,
});

export const Callout = defineComponent({
  name: "Callout",
  description:
    "A boxed aside the source itself sets apart: a warning, a contraindication, " +
    "a key takeaway, a note. Use `tone` to match how the source frames it. Do not " +
    "promote ordinary prose into a Callout for emphasis — reserve it for material " +
    "the source visually distinguishes.",
  props: z.object({
    tone: z
      .enum(["note", "warning", "key", "caveat"])
      .describe("How the source frames this aside."),
    title: z.string().optional().describe("The aside's own heading, if any."),

  component: CalloutBlock,
